---
title: "Invalid relations"
---

This project cannot even produce a graph: one relation points at an object
that does not exist, and one identifier is declared twice. Both are
error-severity findings, and error findings block the snapshot -- there is
nothing safe to publish downstream of them. This is the engine's most
important promise: a broken project fails loudly instead of rendering
half-understood.

::: {.need #REQ-A type="functional-requirement" status="draft"}
## A healthy object

Declared so the project is not minimal to the point of trivia.
:::

::: {.need #REQ-B type="functional-requirement" status="draft" derives-from="REQ-MISSING"}
## Points at a ghost

`derives-from` is a real relation, but REQ-MISSING was never declared -- REQ005.
:::

::: {.need #REQ-D type="functional-requirement" status="draft"}
## First declaration of REQ-D

Identifiers must be unique across the whole project -- REQ004.
:::

::: {.need #REQ-D type="functional-requirement" status="approved"}
## Second declaration of REQ-D

Same ID, different content: the engine refuses to guess which one is real.
:::
